title: MoLing SSE mode exposes local MCP tools to malicious web pages
summary: Unauthenticated SSE endpoints with wildcard CORS let a malicious web page obtain a session identifier and invoke MCP tools. Resulting file access or command execution depends on the configured tools.

severity.rationale: A page can steal the tool session credential and invoke local capabilities. SSE mode and powerful tools are required, so the impact is conditional rather than universal code execution.

exposure: Requires MoLing running in SSE mode and a browser visiting untrusted content.

params.instructions: Check whether MoLing is version 0.4.0 or earlier and runs in SSE mode with the -l flag.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.5.0, which adds token authentication and removes wildcard CORS. Until then avoid SSE mode while exposed to untrusted web content.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm version 0.5.0 or later and verify the SSE endpoint requires authentication and refuses cross-origin access.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Removed the disputed loopback statement from exposure; retained the vendor recommendation to avoid SSE mode with untrusted web content.
